purpose: Compare fixed saved models under common calibration false-alert targets; not a new classifier or a revised training continuation gate
split_rule: SHA256(domain || canonical standardized input fingerprint), first byte even => calibration; odd => audit. Identical float32 input vectors stay together. No label-dependent splitting.
score: Maximum attack logit minus benign logit; subtract in float64 from unchanged float32 logits
prediction: If score > threshold, predict the highest-logit attack category; otherwise Benign. Strict > keeps boundary ties benign. Attack ties use original class order.
threshold: Use only calibration benign scores. Let n be their count, k=floor(n*target_basis_points/10000); threshold is sorted_score[n-k-1]. This is the lowest observed threshold allowing at most k calibration false alerts. No interpolation or random tie breaking.
evaluation: Freeze every method/target threshold from calibration, then evaluate once on the other development half. Report actual audit FAR, all eight classes, confusion matrices and attack detection separately from correct attack classification.
comparison: Primary 5 percent calibration target; compare shared Adam and MIME against selected central Adam and FedAvg at all four targets. Flag pairs whose realized audit FAR differs by more than 0.5 percentage points; do not retune on audit labels or interpolate to force equal audit FAR.
selection: No new learning-rate, checkpoint, architecture, threshold-budget or score selection. Use the five methods already selected by previous full-development macro-F1.
limits: Both halves belong to a previously examined development set used for learning-rate selection; splitting now avoids directly fitting thresholds on audit labels but does not create independent final-test evidence. One training seed and one historical client partition. No IID confidence guarantee or deployment FAR guarantee.
